title: Dashboard link sits after Reports and is the first screen after login
pre: Preconditions You are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin). You open the site in a fresh private (incognito) browser window, so nothing remembered from an earlier visit is in play. You use a desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide (a maximised laptop or desktop window). You are in one location (workplace); write down its name. That location has one invoice created this month (for example 1.00 hour at $100.00). Write down its subtotal (for example $100.00). Setup For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on. For 4: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site try Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. For 5: Customers > New Customer > Name > Save (for example ZZAUTOTEST Entry Fleet); then Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and an Asset (Add beside either if needed) > Save (if a Confirmation says the customer is over their credit limit, click Create); the New Line window opens: What Are You Doing? (any text), Add Technician = a technician (for example Tech ShopView), Labor Rate = EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time 1 and Tech Time 1, tick Line Approved > Save & Close; on the line click Story (Add tech story for this line) > type a short story > Update; click Complete (if a Missing Details window asks for Mileage, enter one > Complete All Lines); click Mark Reviewed; Finance tab > Create Invoice; close the New Customer Payment window without paying (do not send or pay the invoice). The subtotal is on the Finance tab.
steps: Look at the top navigation bar and read the entries from left to right. Click "Dashboard" in the top navigation. Read the location name at the top right (beside your initials) and the Revenue tile's headline. Click the arrow icon beside the word "Revenue" on the Revenue tile (it opens the Sales report on the same range) and read the report's total for that workplace. Sign out (profile icon at the top right > Logout). Sign in again as the same user.
exp: Expected results The top navigation shows a "Dashboard" entry. "Dashboard" sits immediately to the right of "Reports" (with the build's bar: Work Orders, Schedule, Customers, Parts, Reports, Dashboard). Clicking "Dashboard" opens the dashboard screen with its six tiles. The figures are for the workplace shown in the top bar: the Revenue headline (This Month) is not $0.00, it includes the invoice you created (e.g. $100.00), and it equals the Sales report's total for the same workplace and range. After signing in again, the first screen you land on is the dashboard (not Work Orders). Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9573 (Story 1, Dashboard Access and Entry Point); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v48, read 14 Oct 2026, Story 1. Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, as re-shared and read 14 Oct 2026; a screenshot of the SV-490 build re-shot on 14 Oct 2026) board 01_Opens_After (row 1) for the top bar labels.
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S1-R1: “The user sees a "Dashboard" entry in the top navigation.” S1-R5: “The "Dashboard" entry sits immediately to the right of the "Reports" entry.” S1-R2: “When the user selects "Dashboard", the dashboard screen opens.” S1-R4: “The dashboard shows figures for the workplace the user currently has selected in the top navigation.” S1-R3: “When a user who has the Reports permission logs in, the dashboard is the screen they land on.” Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026. title: Login does not open the Dashboard; users land as in Production
pre: Preconditions: A user with the Reports permission (e.g. your admin account). Production available for comparison.
steps: Open Customers, log out, then log back in. Open the Dashboard, log out, then log back in. Open Work Orders, log out, then log back in. While logged out, open a work order link, then log in. While logged out, open a Dashboard link, then log in. Repeat steps 1–4 in Production. As a user without the Reports permission, type the Dashboard address in the browser.
exp: Step 1: Lands on Customers, not the Dashboard. Step 2: Lands on Work Orders (the first page the user’s permissions allow), not the Dashboard. Step 3: Lands on Work Orders. Step 4: The work order opens. Step 5: The Dashboard opens. This is the only case where login ends on the Dashboard. Step 6: The landing page is the same as on Staging for every case. Step 7: Redirected to Work Orders.

pre: Preconditions For the setup you are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission). A staff member whose role has the Reports permission switched off, with access to one location, whose sign-in you have (e.g. ZZAUTOTEST No Reports User with role ZZAUTOTEST No Reports). You have copied the dashboard's web address. Setup For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on. pre: Preconditions You are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin). You are in any location (workplace). title: Switching workplace reloads the dashboard figures
pre: Preconditions You are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin). You open the site in a fresh private (incognito) browser window, so nothing remembered from an earlier visit is in play. Two locations (workplaces) whose figures differ: your normal location (e.g. Staging Heavy Duty - 9919) and one with nothing in it (e.g. ZZAUTOTEST Empty Shop). Setup For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on. For 3: both are in the Change Location list (click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list). If no empty location exists, create one: profile icon > Settings > Locations > New Location: Name (e.g. ZZAUTOTEST Empty Shop), Address 1, City, State/Province, ZIP/Postal Code, Timezone, Telephone > Save & Close; it appears in the Change Location list at once. Create nothing in it.
steps: Change location to your normal location (profile icon > Change Location) and click Dashboard in the top menu. Write down the six tile headlines (e.g. Revenue $2,422.00). Without leaving the dashboard, change location to ZZAUTOTEST Empty Shop (profile icon > Change Location). Read the six tile headlines again. Change location back to your normal location. Look for any way to have no location selected (for example in the Change Location list).

title: Each tile shows the same figure as its matching report
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions User: you are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin). Browser: you use a desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide (a maximised laptop or desktop window). Location: you are in a location (workplace) that has invoices and technician clocked time this month (one day is enough) and over the last twelve months. User: your role can create a work order and an invoice in that location (Admin can).
steps: Click Dashboard in the top menu and leave every tile on its default range. Write down the Revenue headline. Click the arrow icon beside "Revenue" (it opens the Sales report on the same range) and read the report's total for the invoices' subtotals at the foot of the table. Go back to the dashboard, write down the Billing Efficiency headline, then click its arrow icon (Service Advisor Analysis report) and read the report's overall figure with all advisors selected. Go back, write down the Technician Efficiency headline, then click its arrow icon (Technician Efficiency report, Invoiced) and read the overall figure with all technicians selected. Go back, write down the Technician Utilization headline, then click its arrow icon (Technician Utilization report) and read the overall figure with all technicians selected. Go back, write down the Sales by Customer headline, then click its arrow icon (Sales By Customer report) and read how many customers the report lists in total (e.g. the pager reads "1 - 10 of 69"). Create one new invoice in the same location today: Work Orders > Create Work Order > a customer and asset > Save; in New Line add a labor line (e.g. Labor Rate EVR Travel to EVO, $100 an hour, Estimated Time 1) and tick Line Approved > Save & Close; Story > Update; Complete; Mark Reviewed; Finance > Create Invoice. Within one minute, reload the dashboard and read the Revenue headline. Reload the Sales report on the same range and read its total.
exp: Expected results Steps 2 and 3: Revenue equals the Sales report total exactly, to the cent. Steps 4, 5 and 6: Billing Efficiency equals the Service Advisor Analysis figure, Technician Efficiency equals the Technician Efficiency report figure, and Technician Utilization equals the Technician Utilization report figure, each to two decimal places. Step 7: Sales by Customer equals the number of customers the Sales By Customer report lists (e.g. 69 customers and "1 - 10 of 69"). Steps 8, 9 and 10: Straight after the new invoice, both the tile and the report have gone up by the same amount (e.g. $100.00) and still agree. There is no wait, and the tile never shows an older figure than the report. Steps 2 to 10: If any tile and its report disagree at any point, the case fails. Write both figures in the result comment. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (Story 3, Measure Formulas and Report Parity); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v48, read 14 Oct 2026, Story 3. Report links per the Story 10 context note.
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.” S3-N1: “If a measure's report shows a value, the matching tile shows the same value; the two never disagree.” S3 context note (parity check): “to check parity on a KPI tile that shows a shop-wide figure, compare it against the matching report with all advisors or all technicians selected (no filter applied).” Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026. AUTOMATION: READY

title: Each tile's figure matches a hand calculation from known records
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions User: you are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin). Browser: you use a desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide (a maximised laptop or desktop window). Data: the Dash Shop data set exists, all created today in location ZZAUTOTEST Dash Shop, where nothing else is invoiced or clocked this month: work order 1 for customer ZZAUTOTEST Alpha Fleet, Service Advisor ZZAUTOTEST Advisor X, one labor line of 2.00 hours at $100.00 an hour with Tech Time 1.50 and technician ZZAUTOTEST Tech One, a part with Sell Price $50.00, and ZZAUTOTEST Tech One clocked exactly 2.50 hours on it; work order 2 for ZZAUTOTEST Bravo Fleet, Service Advisor ZZAUTOTEST Advisor Y, one labor line of 1.00 hour at $100.00 an hour with Tech Time 1.00 and technicians ZZAUTOTEST Tech One and ZZAUTOTEST Tech Two, a part with Sell Price $160.00, Tech One clocked exactly 0.25 hours and Tech Two exactly 0.75 hours on it. Neither work order has shop supplies, a fee or a discount; both are invoiced and not paid. Totals: invoices $250.00 and $260.00; 3.00 labor hours billed; 2.50 technician hours on the lines; 3.50 clocked hours; no internal (non work order) time. People: ZZAUTOTEST Tech Two belongs to a department whose time clock is on, so they can clock internal (non work order) time.
steps: Click Dashboard in the top menu with ZZAUTOTEST Dash Shop selected and every tile on its default range. Read the Revenue headline and its supporting line. Read the Billing Efficiency headline and its supporting line. Read the Technician Efficiency headline and its supporting line. Read the Technician Utilization headline and its supporting line. Read the Sales by Customer headline. Click View details on Billing Efficiency and read the Advisor Analysis table rows. Click View details on Technician Efficiency and read the table rows. Sign in as ZZAUTOTEST Tech Two in a private window, click Clock In in the top bar, choose the department (not a work order), then clock out. As Admin, set that record to exactly 0.50 hours in Reports > Timesheet Activities (e.g. 15:00 to 15:30 today). Reload the dashboard and read the Technician Utilization headline and supporting line. Click View details on Technician Utilization and read the table rows. Read the At Risk Customers headline. Clean up: delete the 0.50-hour internal record again in Reports > Timesheet Activities, so the data set is back to its base state for other cases.
exp: Expected results Step 2: Revenue reads $510.00 (250.00 + 260.00) with the supporting line "Parts 41% · Labor 59%". Parts are 50.00 + 160.00 = 210.00, and 210 ÷ 510 = 41.2%, so 41%. Labor is 200.00 + 100.00 = 300.00, and 300 ÷ 510 = 58.8%, so 59%. Step 3: Billing Efficiency reads 85.71% with "3.00 Invoiced / 3.50 Clocked" (labor hours billed 2.00 + 1.00 = 3.00; clocked 2.50 + 0.25 + 0.75 = 3.50; 3.00 ÷ 3.50 × 100 = 85.71). Step 4: Technician Efficiency reads 71.43% with "2.50 Invoiced Tech Hrs / 3.50 Clocked" (technician time on the lines 1.50 + 1.00 = 2.50; 2.50 ÷ 3.50 × 100 = 71.43). It differs from Billing Efficiency because technician time is not the same as billed labor hours. Step 7: Advisor Analysis rows: ZZAUTOTEST Advisor X, Worked Hours 2.50, Invoiced Hrs 2.00, Billing Efficiency 80.00%, ELR $80.00 ($200.00 labor ÷ 2.50 hours). ZZAUTOTEST Advisor Y, Worked Hours 1.00, Invoiced Hrs 1.00, Billing Efficiency 100.00%, ELR $100.00 ($100.00 ÷ 1.00). Step 8: Technician Efficiency rows show work order 2's technician time split by each technician's share of the clocked time on that line (Tech One 0.25 of 1.00 clocked = 0.25 hours, Tech Two 0.75 hours). ZZAUTOTEST Tech One: Clocked Hrs 2.75, Invoiced Tech Hrs 1.75 (1.50 + 0.25), Efficiency 63.64%. ZZAUTOTEST Tech Two: Clocked Hrs 0.75, Invoiced Tech Hrs 0.75, Efficiency 100.00%. Step 5: Before the internal time, Technician Utilization reads 100.00% with "3.50 WO Hrs / 3.50 Clocked". Steps 10 and 11: After 0.50 internal hours, Technician Utilization reads 87.50% with "3.50 WO Hrs / 4.00 Clocked" (3.50 ÷ (3.50 + 0.50) × 100 = 87.50). Table: Tech One WO Hours 2.75, Internal Hours 0.00, Total Hours 2.75, Utilization % 100.00%. Tech Two WO Hours 0.75, Internal Hours 0.50, Total Hours 1.25, Utilization % 60.00%. Step 6: Sales by Customer reads "2 customers" (Alpha Fleet and Bravo Fleet, each counted once). Step 12: At Risk Customers reads 0 for this workplace: both customers were invoiced today, so neither invoice is 120 or more days old. Steps 2 to 12: Each figure equals its matching report: Sales, Service Advisor Analysis, Technician Efficiency (Invoiced), Technician Utilization and Sales By Customer. At Risk Customers has no report. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (Story 3, Measure Formulas and Report Parity); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v48, read 14 Oct 2026, Story 3 (requirement S3-R2 and its table). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, as re-shared and read 14 Oct 2026; screenshots of the SV-490 build re-shot on 14 Oct 2026) boards 05_Billing_After, 06_TechEff_After and 07_TechUtil_After for the table columns.
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S3-R2: “Each measure is calculated as defined in the table below.” S3-R2 table: Revenue: “Revenue | Sum of invoice subtotals in the selected range, before any discount and before tax, minus credit memos. Shown to the cent. | Sales report” S3-R2 table: Billing Efficiency: “Billing Efficiency | Invoiced hours divided by worked hours, times 100, for the selected range. | Service Advisor Analysis report” S3-R2 table: Technician Efficiency: “Technician Efficiency | Invoiced technician hours divided by clocked hours, times 100, for the selected range. Each work order line's technician time is split across the technicians who worked it, in proportion to each technician's share of the clocked time on that line. | Technician Efficiency report (Invoiced)” S3-R2 table: Technician Utilization: “Technician Utilization | Work-order hours divided by the sum of work-order hours and internal hours, times 100, for the selected range. | Technician Utilization report” S3-R2 table: Sales by Customer (count): “Sales by Customer (count) | The count of distinct customers with sales in the selected range. | Sales By Customer report” S3-R2 table: At Risk Customers (count): “At Risk Customers (count) | The count of customers whose most recent invoice is at least the selected number of days old, and who also have either two or more lifetime invoices or some revenue in the last twelve months. | None (dashboard-only)” S3-R2 table: ELR (on the Billing Efficiency chart): “ELR (on the Billing Efficiency chart) | Labor sales divided by worked hours, per advisor. | Service Advisor Analysis report” Terminology (worked hours): “the time technicians actually clocked, from their time records.” Terminology (invoiced technician hours): “the technician time recorded on work order lines. Used by Technician Efficiency. This is a different figure from invoiced hours.” Terminology (internal hours): “clocked time not tied to a work order, such as internal tasks.” S3 context note (At Risk): “At Risk Customers has no report, so parity does not apply to it; its formula in this table is the only definition of the measure.” Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026. title: Ratio tiles with no clocked hours show a grey dash, not 0.00%
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions User: you are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin). Browser: you use a desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide (a maximised laptop or desktop window). Location: you are in a location (workplace) with no clocked time at all and nothing else in it yet (for example ZZAUTOTEST No Clock Shop).
steps: Click Dashboard in the top menu and leave every tile on This Month. Read the Billing Efficiency, Technician Efficiency and Technician Utilization headlines and their colour. Read the Revenue supporting line. Create one invoiced work order in this location with no clocked time: Customers > New Customer (e.g. ZZAUTOTEST No Clock Fleet) > Save; Work Orders > Create Work Order > that customer and an asset > Save; in New Line: Add Technician, Labor Rate EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time 1 and Tech Time 1, tick Line Approved > Save & Close, and do not let anyone clock in; Story > Update; Complete; Mark Reviewed; Finance > Create Invoice. Reload the dashboard and read the three ratio headlines again. Click the arrow icon beside "Billing Efficiency" and read the Service Advisor Analysis figure for the same range.
exp: Expected results Step 2: With no clocked hours, each of the three ratio tiles shows exactly "-": a single hyphen, in grey. None of them shows "0.00%", "0%" or "n/a". Step 3: With no revenue, the Revenue tile's supporting line shows the invoice count instead of a parts and labor split (e.g. "0 Invoices"). Step 5: After invoicing a line with technician time but no clocked time, the three ratio headlines still read "-" in grey. Nothing breaks: no error, no endless number, and no blank tile. Step 6: The report may show its empty figure differently (an empty number with a % sign). That difference alone does not fail this case. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (Story 3, Measure Formulas and Report Parity); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v48, read 14 Oct 2026, Story 3 (S3-E3 and its context note). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, as re-shared and read 14 Oct 2026; a screenshot of the SV-490 build re-shot on 14 Oct 2026) board 15_Empty_After (row 15): the three ratio tiles read a grey "-".
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S3-E3: “Billing Efficiency, Technician Efficiency and Technician Utilization are each a ratio. When the denominator for the selected range is zero, worked hours, clocked hours, or the sum of work-order and internal hours, the measure has no value for that range. It is not zero, and the tile must not show "0.00%", because no hours recorded and a genuine zero percent are different facts. The same applies to the Revenue tile's parts-versus-labor split when revenue for the range is zero (S4-N2 already gives that tile its fallback supporting line). Inside the Technician Efficiency calculation, a work order line with invoiced technician time but no clocked time contributes no split share rather than an infinite one. The tile headline reads exactly "-", a single hyphen, in grey.” S3-E3 context note: “the matching report renders its own empty cell differently, as an empty number with the percent sign still shown. Bringing the report's empty state into line is deliberately outside this spec, so a difference between the tile and the report in this one case, where neither is showing a figure, is not a failure of the parity rule in S3-R1. S3-R1 governs the figures.” Last checked against build v26.40.8-754bd3a on 10/13/2026. AUTOMATION: READY

title: Revenue shows a negative figure when credits exceed sales
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions User: you are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin). Location: That location has an invoice from an earlier day with a part on it (e.g. a part with Sell Price $160.00).
steps: On that earlier invoice: Finance tab > the invoice's three-dot menu > Issue Credit. In the Issue Credit window, under Parts to return pick the part (e.g. the $160.00 part) and keep Parts are being returned ticked; under Outcome choose Issue Store Credit; click Issue Credit. Click Dashboard in the top menu. On the Revenue tile, open the range pill, pick today only in the calendar (click today twice) and click Apply. Read the headline (the large figure) on the Revenue tile. Click the arrow icon beside "Revenue" and read the Sales report total for the same range.
exp: Expected results Step 5: The Revenue headline shows the true negative figure, e.g. "-$160.00" (sales today $0.00 minus credits today $160.00). It does not show $0.00. src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S3-E1: “The Revenue figure can be negative when credit memos in the range exceed sales; the dashboard shows the true negative figure rather than flooring it at zero.” S7-R2a: “The control is the same date picker the reports use. title: A voided invoice is left out of every dashboard figure
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions User: you are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin). Browser: you use a desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide (a maximised laptop or desktop window). Location: a location for the void check exists (for example ZZAUTOTEST Void Shop) with two invoices, not paid and not sent: customer ZZAUTOTEST Keep Fleet, one labor line of 1.00 hour at $100.00 an hour with Tech Time 1.00 and exactly 1.00 hour clocked on it; customer ZZAUTOTEST Void Fleet, one labor line of 2.00 hours at $150.00 an hour (e.g. $300.00) with Tech Time 2.00 and nobody clocked on it. User: you can switch to a location with at-risk customers, and you have written down one at-risk customer's name and Last Invoice Date (Dashboard > View details on At Risk Customers).
steps: With ZZAUTOTEST Void Shop selected, click Dashboard in the top menu (all tiles on their defaults) and write down every headline and supporting line. Void the Void Fleet invoice: on that work order's Lines tab add a New Line (any small line) while the invoice is still unpaid and unsent. The Finance tab now shows the invoice as voided. Do not create a new invoice. Reload the dashboard and read every headline and supporting line again. Change location to the location with the at-risk customer (profile icon > Change Location), click Dashboard in the top menu and write down the At Risk headline. Create a new work order for that customer: Work Orders > Create Work Order > the customer and an asset > Save; in New Line one labor line (e.g. Labor Rate EVR Travel to EVO, Estimated Time 0.5), tick Line Approved > Save & Close; Story > Update; Complete; Mark Reviewed; Finance > Create Invoice (do not pay or send). Reload the dashboard and read the At Risk headline. Void that invoice the same way (add a New Line on its Lines tab). Reload the dashboard, click View details on At Risk Customers and find the customer.
exp: Expected results Step 1: Before the void (step 1): Revenue $400.00 (100.00 + 300.00), "2 customers", Billing Efficiency 300.00% (3.00 invoiced hours ÷ 1.00 clocked hour) and Technician Efficiency 300.00% (3.00 ÷ 1.00). Step 3: After the void, the voided invoice contributes nothing. Revenue $100.00 and its Parts/Labor split "Parts 0% · Labor 100%". Billing Efficiency 100.00% with "1.00 Invoiced / 1.00 Clocked". Technician Efficiency 100.00% with "1.00 Invoiced Tech Hrs / 1.00 Clocked". Sales by Customer "1 customer" (Void Fleet no longer counted). Step 3: The matching reports (Sales, Service Advisor Analysis, Technician Efficiency, Sales By Customer) leave the voided invoice out in the same way. Step 6: While the at-risk customer's new invoice was live, they dropped out of At Risk (the headline went down by 1). Step 8: After that invoice is voided, the customer is back in the At Risk table with their old Last Invoice Date (e.g. Oct 10, 2025): the voided invoice is not treated as their most recent invoice. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (Story 3, Measure Formulas and Report Parity); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v48, read 14 Oct 2026, Story 3. How to produce a voided invoice by hand comes from the Technical Implementation Plan (2026-09-16) section 7: an invoice is voided by adding a line while it is still pending; reversing an invoice deletes it rather than voiding it.
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S3-E2: “A voided invoice is excluded from every figure the dashboard shows. It contributes nothing to Revenue or to the parts-versus-labor split, nothing to invoiced hours or invoiced technician hours, and it is counted in neither the Sales by Customer count nor the At Risk Customers count, including when deciding a customer's most recent invoice. This is not a dashboard rule of its own: it is what the reports do, and the dashboard matches them (S3-R1). A void means the document was undone, so a figure that still carried its money or its hours would overstate the shop.” Last checked against build v26.40.8-754bd3a on 10/13/2026. AUTOMATION: READY

title: Revenue and Billing Efficiency tiles show the right headline and line
pre: Signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission — the Administrator storage state of the `dashboard` project; desktop window at least 1024px wide A busy location with invoices and technician clocked time over the last twelve months: the session's own workplace, seeded via API — one minted billable technician and one invoiced work order dated today with a labour line, the technician clocked 1.00 h on it (yesterday) — and read through the dashboard endpoint: Revenue and Technician Efficiency's clocked hours over Last 12 Months both above zero The Dash Shop data set, seeded via API today at "E2E Dashboard Dash Shop" (found or created, admin enrolled; this month's figures read back as zero first): WO 1 (customer "Alpha Fleet", Advisor X, labour 2.00 h fixed $200.00 with Tech Time 1.50, one $50.00 part, Tech One clocked 2.50 h) and WO 2 (customer "Bravo Fleet", Advisor Y, labour 1.00 h fixed $100.00 with Tech Time 1.00, one $160.00 part, a flat $10.00 shop supplies charge, Tech One 0.25 h + Tech Two 0.75 h), both invoiced and unpaid; no internal time; read through the dashboard endpoint: Revenue $520.00 split Parts 40% · Labor 58% · Other 2%
steps: With your busy location selected, click Dashboard in the top menu and look at each of the four tiles in the top row. Hover the arrow icon beside each tile's name. Change location to ZZAUTOTEST Dash Shop (profile icon > Change Location). Read the Revenue headline and supporting line. Read the Billing Efficiency headline and supporting line.
exp: Expected results Each of the four top tiles shows its name (label), a headline value, a small trend line, a date-range pill (e.g. "This Month") and an arrow icon beside the name that links to its report. A tile with fewer than two days of figures shows a dashed outline with a chart icon instead of the trend line; that is expected and covered by its own case. Revenue reads "$510.00": a dollar amount with two decimals (250.00 + 260.00). Revenue's supporting line reads "Parts 41% · Labor 59%", whole numbers with no decimals that add up to 100 (210 ÷ 510 = 41.2%, so 41%; 300 ÷ 510 = 58.8%, so 59%). There is no "Other" share, because these invoices have no shop supplies or fees. Billing Efficiency reads "85.71%", two decimal places (3.00 ÷ 3.50 × 100). Billing Efficiency's supporting line reads "3.00 Invoiced / 3.50 Clocked". Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9576 (Story 4, KPI Hero Tiles); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v50 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 16 Oct 2026, Story 4. Design canvas boards 01_Opens_After and 02_Last12_After for the tile layout (arrow icon, range pill).
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S4-R1: “Each KPI tile shows a label, a headline value, a sparkline, a date-range control, and a report link.” S4-R2: “The Revenue tile headline is the total revenue for the selected range, shown as a dollar amount to the cent.” S4-R3: “The Revenue tile shows a supporting line reading "Parts {parts}% · Labor {labor}% · Other {other}%", each percent a whole number of the tile’s revenue. Parts is parts sales, net of credits (as today). Labor is labor sales only, the same figure as the Sales report’s Labor column. Other is everything else in revenue: shop supplies, fees and any other line that is neither a part nor labor. The three are rounded so they always add up to 100. "· Other {other}%" is left off when Other rounds to 0%, so a shop with no supplies or fees reads "Parts {parts}% · Labor {labor}%".” S4-R4: “The Billing Efficiency tile headline is the billing efficiency percentage for the selected range, shown to two decimal places.” S4-R5: “The Billing Efficiency tile shows a supporting line reading "{invoiced hours} Invoiced / {clocked hours} Clocked".” Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026, before the expected results changed on 16 Oct 2026; the changed results have not yet been checked against a build. title: The small trend line uses days, weeks or months by range length
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), whose role has the Reports permission, at location {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). Your browser window is at least 1024 pixels wide at 100% zoom (a maximised laptop or desktop window). {Location-A} has invoices spread over the last twelve months, so the Revenue tile shows an amount above $0.00 on Last 12 Months. This month, at least two days at {Location-A} have clocked time on invoiced work, with a day between them that has no clocked time at all, {Day-A} (for example a Sunday).
steps: Click Dashboard in the top bar. Click the Revenue tile's date pill, pick a start day and an end day in the calendar so the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 31 days", and click Apply. Count the points (corners) on the Revenue trend line. Click the Revenue tile's date pill, pick a start day and an end day in the calendar so the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 32 days", and click Apply. Count the points. Click the Revenue tile's date pill, pick a start day and an end day in the calendar so the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 182 days", and click Apply. Count the points. Click the Revenue tile's date pill, pick a start day and an end day in the calendar so the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 183 days", and click Apply. Count the points. Set the Revenue pill to Last 12 Months and click View details on Revenue. Compare the Revenue trend line's shape with the monthly bars in the Revenue chart. Set the Billing Efficiency pill to This Month and look at its trend line at {Day-A}.
exp: Expected results Step 3: 31 days draws exactly 31 points, one for every day, including days with no sales: on Revenue a day with no sales is a point at $0, not a gap. Step 4: 32 days draws one point per week (about 5 points). Step 5: 182 days still draws one point per week (about 26 points). Step 6: 183 days draws one point per month (about 7 points). Steps 7 and 8: On Last 12 Months the trend line has 12 points, and they rise and fall exactly like the 12 monthly bars in the expanded Revenue chart. No point disagrees with the bar for the same month. Step 9: {Day-A} has no point on the Billing Efficiency line: the day has no value, so nothing is drawn for it, and it is not drawn down to zero. The line runs straight from the day before {Day-A} to the day after it, in one line across the full width of the tile. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9576 (Story 4, KPI Hero Tiles), with SV-9579 (Story 7), SV-9578 (Story 6) and SV-9581 (Story 9); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850, version 48 (14 Oct 2026, 17:09 UTC, Chris Ward), S4-R10 and S4-R11 (unchanged since version 42), S4-R11a (added in version 43 on 9 Oct 2026), S7-R2a, S6-R3a and S9-R9 (added in version 45 on 14 Oct 2026 (15:06 UTC) by Chris Ward; the spec's change log (version 46) lists it under 2026-10-14); read 14 Oct 2026. The 731-day and 732-day ranges were removed because a tile's calendar now allows at most 366 days (S7-R2a, Chris Ward's answer 3 of 14 Oct 2026), so the switch to one point per quarter cannot be reached from a tile. Step 9 follows Story Defect SV-11328 (Chris Ward's decision, Slack 15 Oct 2026: the sparkline always runs fully left to right across the tile), which replaces S4-R11's "interior gaps are preserved" until the PRD is updated. Design canvas board 03_Range_After for the date pill, calendar and "Range: N days" readout. Source-verified 14 October 2026. This version of the case has not yet been checked against a build.
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S4-R10: “The sparkline shows the tile's measure trending over the selected range.” S4-R11: “The sparkline draws one point per bucket, and the bucket size is chosen from the length of the selected range: a range of 31 days or fewer buckets by day; 32 to 182 days by week; 183 to 731 days by month; anything longer by quarter. Each point is the measure recomputed over that bucket using the same calculation as the headline, so a point can never disagree with the tile it sits in. A bucket for which the measure has no value (S3-E3) contributes no point, and interior gaps are preserved rather than closed up or drawn as zero. When fewer than two points have values, no line is drawn and the tile shows the empty-chart placeholder instead (S4-R12).” S4-R11a: “On Revenue and the count tiles, a bucket with no sales is a point at 0. Only a ratio tile's "-" (S3-E3) contributes no point.” S7-R2a: “The control is the same date picker the reports use. Besides the nine presets it offers a calendar for choosing a custom range of up to 366 days, the same limit the reports apply, and a Today button inside the calendar. Today is part of the calendar, not a tenth preset. A custom range is not remembered between visits (S7-R8), and the report opened from the tile shows it as "Custom" (S10-E1).” S6-R3a: “The expanded Revenue chart covers the tile's own date range (S7-R5), with one bar per day, week, month or quarter chosen from the length of the range by the same rule as the sparkline (S4-R11). Last 12 Months shows twelve monthly bars; This Month shows daily bars.” S9-R9: “In an expanded chart, a month with no value is drawn as a dashed line joining the points on either side of it. This is how these charts already draw in production. A gap in the line applies only to the sparkline on a tile (S4-R11).” AUTOMATION: READY

title: KPI tiles show exact figures with no change indicator
pre: Preconditions You are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin). title: Sales by Customer tile counts customers and names the top one
pre: Preconditions You are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin). You use a desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide (a maximised laptop or desktop window). A location with exactly one customer sold to exists (for example ZZAUTOTEST One Customer Shop): one invoice, not paid, for customer ZZAUTOTEST Solo Fleet (for example 1.00 hour at $100.00). The Dash Shop data set exists, all created today in location ZZAUTOTEST Dash Shop, where nothing else is invoiced or clocked this month: work order 1 for customer ZZAUTOTEST Alpha Fleet, Service Advisor ZZAUTOTEST Advisor X, one labor line of 2.00 hours at $100.00 an hour with Tech Time 1.50 and technician ZZAUTOTEST Tech One, a part with Sell Price $50.00, and ZZAUTOTEST Tech One clocked exactly 2.50 hours on it; work order 2 for ZZAUTOTEST Bravo Fleet, Service Advisor ZZAUTOTEST Advisor Y, one labor line of 1.00 hour at $100.00 an hour with Tech Time 1.00 and technicians ZZAUTOTEST Tech One and ZZAUTOTEST Tech Two, a part with Sell Price $160.00, Tech One clocked exactly 0.25 hours and Tech Two exactly 0.75 hours on it. Neither work order has shop supplies, a fee or a discount; both are invoiced and not paid. Totals: invoices $250.00 and $260.00; 3.00 labor hours billed; 2.50 technician hours on the lines; 3.50 clocked hours; no internal (non work order) time. Setup For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on. For 3: profile icon > Settings > Locations > New Location: Name ZZAUTOTEST One Customer Shop, the address fields, Timezone, Telephone, Shop Supplies Charge 0 % > Save & Close (if a location with this name already exists, reuse it only if it still matches the precondition). It then appears in your Change Location list; to switch to it, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list; switch to it; Customers > New Customer > Name > Save (ZZAUTOTEST Solo Fleet); Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and an Asset (Add beside either if needed) > Save (if a Confirmation says the customer is over their credit limit, click Create); the New Line window opens: What Are You Doing? (any text), Add Technician = a technician (for example Tech ShopView), Labor Rate = EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time 1 and Tech Time 1, tick Line Approved > Save & Close; on the line click Story (Add tech story for this line) > type a short story > Update; click Complete (if a Missing Details window asks for Mileage, enter one > Complete All Lines); click Mark Reviewed; Finance tab > Create Invoice; close the New Customer Payment window without paying (do not send or pay the invoice). For 4: if ZZAUTOTEST Dash Shop already exists with exactly this data, reuse it. Otherwise: (a) location: profile icon > Settings > Locations > New Location: Name ZZAUTOTEST Dash Shop, the address fields, Timezone, Telephone, Shop Supplies Charge 0 % > Save & Close (if a location with this name already exists, reuse it only if it still matches the precondition). It then appears in your Change Location list; to switch to it, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. (b) staff: profile icon > Settings > Staff > New Staff Member, four times: ZZAUTOTEST Tech One and ZZAUTOTEST Tech Two with Role Technician and Time Clock on, ZZAUTOTEST Advisor X and ZZAUTOTEST Advisor Y with Role Service Advisor; each with Location ZZAUTOTEST Dash Shop and a Department > Save & Close. Give each technician an email address you can open: they must accept the invitation email and set a password so you can sign in as them in a private window. (c) customers: Customers > New Customer > Name > Save, for ZZAUTOTEST Alpha Fleet and ZZAUTOTEST Bravo Fleet. (d) each work order: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and an Asset (Add beside either if needed) > Save (if a Confirmation says the customer is over their credit limit, click Create); the New Line window opens: What Are You Doing? (any text), Add Technician = the technician(s), Labor Rate = EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time and Tech Time as above, tick Line Approved > Save & Close; set Service Advisor in the work order's left panel; on the line click Add Part and add a part with the Sell Price above (it must show In stock, or be ordered and received, before you can invoice). (e) clocked time: sign in as each technician in a private window > open the work order > on the line's Labor row click Start, then Stop > Clock Out; then, as Admin, the three dots at the top right of the Lines tab > Timesheets (n) > edit the record's start and end (if it cannot be edited there or in Reports > Timesheet Activities, keep the real time and use the hours Timesheet Activities shows). (f) on each work order: on the line click Story (Add tech story for this line) > type a short story > Update; click Complete (if a Missing Details window asks for Mileage, enter one > Complete All Lines); click Mark Reviewed; Finance tab > Create Invoice; close the New Customer Payment window without paying (do not send or pay the invoice).
steps: Change location to ZZAUTOTEST One Customer Shop (profile icon > Change Location) and click Dashboard in the top menu. Read the Sales by Customer headline and supporting line. Change location to ZZAUTOTEST Dash Shop (profile icon > Change Location). Read the Sales by Customer headline and supporting line. Set the tile back to Last 12 Months and look at the trend line. Hover the arrow icon beside "Sales by Customer". Click the arrow icon.
exp: Expected results In ZZAUTOTEST One Customer Shop the headline reads "1 customer" (singular) and the supporting line reads "Top: ZZAUTOTEST Solo Fleet". In ZZAUTOTEST Dash Shop the headline reads "2 customers": distinct customers with sales in the range, each counted once. The supporting line reads "Top: " followed by a customer name with sales in the range (e.g. "Top: ZZAUTOTEST Bravo Fleet"). Write down which name shows. The tile has its own range pill. It opens on Last 12 Months and changing it changes only this tile. On Last 12 Months the trend line has one point per month. title: At Risk count, its twelve-month trend line and the remembered window
pre: Preconditions You are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example Admin). You use a desktop browser window at least 1024 pixels wide (a maximised laptop or desktop window). You are in a location (workplace) with at-risk customers. In that location's At Risk table (Dashboard > View details on At Risk Customers) there are two customers whose invoices are inside the last twelve months: Customer A with Lifetime Invoices 1 and a parts-only invoice (e.g. Revenue (12 Mo) $40.50), and Customer B with Lifetime Invoices 2 or more. You have written down both names and the At Risk headline. Setup For 1: on the QA site's sign-in page, in the DEV MODE — QUICK LOGIN panel, click Admin (this signs you in as Admin ShopView). To use another role, check it has Reports: profile icon > Settings > Roles & Permissions > edit icon on the role > Reports is switched on. For 3: to change location, click your profile icon (your initials, top right, beside the current location name) > under Change Location: click the orange button showing the current location > pick the location from the list. On the QA site try Staging Heavy Duty - 9919. Check: the At Risk Customers tile shows a number above 0. If not, try the other locations in the list. If no location in the list passes this check, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no location has this data. For 4: read the table's Lifetime Invoices and Revenue (12 Mo) columns; to see whether an invoice has only parts: Customers > the customer > Invoices tab (turn Open only off). Invoices cannot be back-dated, so if no such customers exist, mark the case Blocked and write in the result comment that no such customers exist.
steps: Count the points on the At Risk trend line and compare its last point with the headline. On Customer A's invoice (Customers > Customer A > its work order > Finance tab > invoice three-dot menu > Issue Credit), credit every part on it and submit. Reload the dashboard and read the At Risk headline. Look for Customer A in the table. Credit every part on Customer B's latest invoice the same way. Reload the dashboard and look for Customer B in the table. Change the window pill to 60 days. Close the browser tab, open the site again in the same browser and open the dashboard. Click Dashboard in the top menu in a private window. Change your computer's time zone to one several hours away (computer settings > Date & Time), reload the dashboard and read the At Risk headline. Then set the time zone back.
exp: Expected results The trend line has twelve points, one per month over the last twelve months. Its last point sits at the same level as the headline. Exact point values cannot be read off the trend line by hand: write 'point values not read' in the result comment. After Customer A's twelve-month revenue drops to $0.00 (one lifetime invoice, no revenue above $0.00), Customer A is no longer at risk. The headline goes down by 1 and they leave the table. Customer B stays in the table after their twelve-month revenue drops to $0.00, because they still have two or more lifetime invoices. Back in the same browser, the pill still reads 60 days (remembered). In the private window it reads 120 Days (the default), because the choice is kept only in the browser where it was made. Changing the computer's time zone does not change the At Risk headline: days are counted in the shop's own time zone. That the count changes at the shop's own midnight cannot be checked by hand; write 'midnight change not checked by hand' in the result comment. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9577 (Story 5, Count Tiles, Sales by Customer and At Risk Customers); story SV-9578 (Story 6, Expanding a Tile); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, Story 5 and Story 6 (S6-R16). Design canvas boards 09_AtRisk_Window and 09_AtRisk_After (row 9).
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S5-R13: “The At Risk Customers sparkline shows the at-risk count over the trailing twelve months as twelve monthly points. Each historical point is the at-risk count as of the last day of that month in the workplace's timezone, using the inactivity window the tile currently shows. The twelfth point is computed as of now, rather than as of a month end that has not happened yet, so it always equals the headline. Every point is recomputed from current data, so a later void changes the past points: recording the count as it stood at the time would contradict S3-E2, which excludes a voided invoice even when deciding a customer's most recent invoice.” S5-R14: “The inactivity window the user chose is remembered and applied on their next visit, in place of the 120-day default (S5-R11), under the storage rule in S6-R16.” S5-R15: “Two parts of the at-risk definition are fixed here so the count cannot be read two ways. "Some revenue in the last twelve months" means revenue greater than $0.00 over the trailing twelve months, measured the way the Revenue tile measures revenue: invoice subtotals before any discount and before tax, minus credit memos. A customer whose twelve-month revenue is exactly $0.00, or is negative because credits exceeded sales, does not satisfy this part of the test, though they can still qualify on the two-or-more-lifetime-invoices part. "At least the selected number of days old" is counted in whole calendar days in the selected workplace's timezone, from the date of the customer's most recent invoice to the current date. The count therefore changes at the shop's own midnight and is stable through the shop's working day, and two people viewing the same workplace from different places see the same number.” Terminology (at-risk customer): “a customer who has bought before but whose most recent invoice is at least the selected number of days old (the inactivity window), and who also has either two or more lifetime invoices or some revenue in the last twelve months.” Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026. The $ amount equals the sum of Revenue (12 Mo) over all at-risk customers, every row on every page (e.g. $40.50 + $1,209.50 = $1,250.00). It is not the sum of the first page only. If the table ever stops at 500 rows (it then says "Showing 500 of N at-risk customers"), the $ amount still covers all N customers. Also the Technical Implementation Plan (2026-09-16), FR-016 and the response contract, which add that the total is never a sum of the displayed rows.
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S5 context note (At Risk revenue): “in the At Risk supporting line, "${revenue} (12mo)" is the customer's revenue over the last twelve months; for more than one customer it is the total across all at-risk customers.” S5-R9: “The At Risk Customers tile shows a supporting line reading "${revenue} (12mo) · {count} customers" when more than one customer is at risk.” S6-R8: “The At Risk Customers tile expands to the At Risk Customers table. The table is ordered by each customer's trailing-twelve-month revenue, highest first, with the customer name as the tiebreaker, so the largest amount at risk reads first. The table lists every at-risk customer. A safety cap of 500 rows applies: if a workplace ever exceeds it, the table shows the first 500 in that order and says so on screen, reading "Showing 500 of N at-risk customers", while the headline still counts every one. The table never truncates silently, because a table that stops short while the headline counts more is a defect: the two then disagree.” Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026. title: Tiles load on their own and remember choices in this browser
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions User: you are signed in as a user whose role has the Reports permission (for example an Administrator). Browser: your browser window is at least 1024 pixels wide (a maximised laptop or desktop window). Location: you are in a location (workplace) that has invoices and technician clocked time on several different days this month and in the last twelve months. steps: Click Dashboard in the top menu and watch the tiles while they load. On the Revenue tile change the range pill to Last Year and watch the tile straight away. Click View details on Technician Utilization. In its chart, open the "Technician: All technicians" filter and untick all but one technician. Set the At Risk window to 60 days. Open Reports > Sales and click Hide Chart above the report table. Close the tab, open the site again in the same browser and open the dashboard, then Reports > Sales. Open the dashboard and Reports > Sales in the second browser (or a private window). In the first browser clear the site's data (browser settings > privacy > clear browsing data for this site), sign in again and open the dashboard.
exp: Expected results Steps 1 and 2: While loading, each tile shows a placeholder in place of its headline, supporting line and trend line. Its name and pills stay readable. No tile is ever blank and no tile shows the old range's figure while the new one loads. If loading is too quick to see, write 'loading state not seen' in the result comment. Step 1: The tiles appear one by one as each finishes. No toast or pop-up message appears. Step 1: A tile whose figures cannot be loaded shows that it could not load while the other five still show their figures. There is no way to make one tile fail by hand: this part cannot be checked by hand; write 'not checked by hand' in the result comment and pass or fail on what you can see. Step 7: Back in the same browser, the Technician Utilization panel is still open, the one-technician filter is kept, At Risk still reads 60 days and the Sales report's chart is still hidden. Step 8: In the second browser or private window, all of these are back to their defaults: no tile open, all technicians, 120 Days, chart shown. They are not part of the user's account. Step 9: After clearing the site's data, every one of them is back to its default. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9578 (Story 6, Expanding a Tile); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v48, read 14 Oct 2026, Story 6. Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, as re-shared and read 14 Oct 2026; a screenshot of the SV-8311 build captured 2026-09-28, unchanged) board 10_sales_Hidden (row 10) for Hide Chart.
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S6-R14: “A tile whose figures have not arrived shows a placeholder in place of its headline, supporting line and sparkline, and its label and controls remain readable. The dashboard never shows a blank tile and never shows a stale figure from a previous range while a new one loads.” S6-R15: “The tiles load independently. A tile whose data cannot be loaded shows that it could not load, and the other five tiles still render their own figures. One failed tile never blanks the dashboard, and the dashboard shows no toast or alert for it (§7).” S6-R16: “Every choice the dashboard remembers, the expanded tile, a chart's technician or advisor selection (S8-R6), the At Risk inactivity window (S5-R14), and the show-or-hide state of an embedded chart (S11-E1), is stored in the browser. It is therefore per browser and per device: it does not follow the user to another computer, another browser, or a private window, and it is not part of the user's account. Clearing browser data returns every one of them to its default.” Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026. AUTOMATION: READY

A bucket for which the measure has no value (S3-E3) contributes no point, and interior gaps are preserved rather than closed up or drawn as zero. When fewer than two points have values, no line is drawn and the tile shows the empty-chart placeholder instead (S4-R12).” S10-R8: “"Last 12 months" covers the same window on every tile and in every report the dashboard links to: from the first day of the month eleven months before the current month, through today, in the workplace's timezone. Every visit opens each tile on its default from S7-R7, which is why date ranges are absent from the remembered list in S6-R16. title: One very high value caps the percentage axis at 200%
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions User: you are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports). Location: you are in one location (workplace) with the data below. Browser: you use a desktop browser at 100% zoom on a screen at least 1024 pixels wide (any ordinary laptop or desktop monitor). Data: a one-off very high Billing Efficiency month for one advisor exists: one invoiced work order today whose Service Advisor has nothing else invoiced this month, with one labor line of 1.00 hour assigned to a technician who clocked exactly 0.25 hours on it (1.00 / 0.25 x 100 = 400%). Location: the location also has other advisors with ordinary monthly figures under 200% over the last twelve months, so most plotted points are at or below 200%.
steps: Click Dashboard in the top bar. Set the Billing Efficiency pill to Last 12 Months. Click View details on the Billing Efficiency tile. Hover each point and count how many read 200% or less and how many read more than 200%. Read the top label of the left-hand axis. Hover the point of the advisor seeded above for this month (it sits at the very top edge).
exp: Expected results Step 4: Most points read 200% or less (e.g. 60 of 62 points), and at least one reads above 200%. Step 5: The axis tops out at 200%: its highest label reads 200%. Step 6: The very high point is drawn clipped at the top edge of the chart (its line runs off the top), but hovering it shows its true value, e.g. 400%. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9581 (Story 9, Chart Behavior); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v48, read 14 Oct 2026, Story 9. Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, as re-shared and read 14 Oct 2026; a screenshot of the SV-490 build re-shot on 14 Oct 2026) board 05_Billing_After, used for on-screen labels only (its re-shot data stays below 200%, so it no longer shows the capped axis; the cap comes from the PRD alone).
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S9-R2: “When one value is far above the rest — a value above 200% while the median of the values stays at or below 200% — the axis caps at 200% so the rest of the data stays readable. The median is taken over every plotted value on the chart, pooled across all of its drawn lines rather than computed per line, counting only points that have a value; where the number of points is even it is the mean of the two middle values. When the highest value on the chart is at or below 200% the axis simply fits the data and no cap applies.” S9-R2: “When one value is far above the rest — a value above 200% while the median of the values stays at or below 200% — the axis caps at 200% so the rest of the data stays readable. The median is taken over every plotted value on the chart, pooled across all of its drawn lines rather than computed per line, counting only points that have a value; where the number of points is even it is the mean of the two middle values. pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), whose role has the Reports permission, at location {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). Click Technician Utilization in the left menu, set the Date control to Last 12 months and hover {Technician-A}'s name in the legend.

title: Dashboard tiles load quickly and one slow tile does not hold up the others
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions User: you are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports). Location: you are in the busiest location (workplace) you can reach: the one with the most invoices and clocked time, so every tile has real work to do. Before you start: you have a stopwatch or a phone timer ready.
steps: Click Work Orders in the top menu so you start away from the Dashboard. Start the stopwatch and click Dashboard in the top menu. Stop the stopwatch when all six tiles (Revenue, Billing Efficiency, Technician Efficiency, Technician Utilization, Sales by Customer, At Risk Customers) show a figure. Write down the time. On each of the four top tiles and on Sales by Customer, click the range pill and choose Last 12 Months. Watch the tiles while each one reloads and note whether any tile stays blank or waits for another tile. Repeat steps 1 to 4 two more times and write down each time.
exp: Expected results Steps 3, 4 and 7: Each time, all six tiles show their figures in about one second. A load that clearly takes several seconds, again and again, is reported. Step 6: The tiles fill in on their own: no tile waits for another tile before it shows its figure. Steps 2 to 7: This part cannot be checked by hand: the measured targets (95 of every 100 first loads within 1 second, each tile's server time within 250 ms, no single query over 500 ms, and a 2-second cut-off that fails only the slow tile). Write "targets not checked by hand" in the result comment and pass or fail on what you can see. Step 6: Making one tile slow or fail on purpose is not possible by hand. Write "slow-tile cut-off not checked by hand" in the result comment. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; Dashboard v1 Technical Implementation Plan (sources/Dashboard-v1-Technical-Implementation-Plan.md, 2026-09-16), NFR-001, read in full 7 Oct 2026. The tech plan informs and never overrules the PRD; Dashboard v1 PRD Confluence 788430850 v48 (read 14 Oct 2026) states no speed target.
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) Tech plan NFR-001: “No dashboard query may exceed 500 ms; anything above is treated as a defect and alerted. Per-tile server time targets p95 ≤ 250 ms; the six-tile first load targets p95 ≤ 1 s (a slight overrun is acceptable). Every dashboard statement carries a 2 s `MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` circuit breaker, and a query that trips it fails only its own tile (FR-021)” Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026. title: Sales and Advisor Analysis reports drop a voided invoice and keep its re-invoice
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), whose role has the Reports permission and can create and invoice work orders. Location {Location-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Quiet 14 Oct A) is a fresh location made for this run: nothing else is invoiced, credited or clocked there, so on the Dashboard the Revenue tile on This Week reads $0.00 with 0 Invoices. Labor rate {Rate-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Rate 100) charges $100.00 an hour at {Location-A}. Customer {Customer-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST C88632 Void Reinvoice) has one contact and one asset (for example unit ZZ-101). {User-A} has Time Clock on and is the technician on the work. Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S490-1201) for {Customer-A} is invoiced, not sent and not paid, and its Service Advisor is {User-A}. {Work-order-1} has one labor line, {Line-1} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST Line 1"), with technician {User-A}, labor rate {Rate-A}, Estimated Time 2.00 and Tech Time 2.00, and exactly 2.00 hours clocked on it. You have written down the invoice's Subtotal (for example $200.00). You run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record stays inside This Week. You can open the release notes page on Confluence (https://shopview.atlassian.net/wiki/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=931069964).
steps: Click Reports in the top menu, then Sales in the left menu. Set the Date control to This week. Write down the row for {Work-order-1}'s invoice and the Subtotal in the Totals row. Click Advisor Analysis in the left menu (the page is titled Service Advisor Analysis) and set the Date control to This week, with no advisor chosen. Write down the invoice's row: Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Billing Efficiency, ELR and Subtotal. Click Work Orders in the top menu and open {Work-order-1}. On the Lines tab click New Line and add a second line: What Are You Doing? (for example "ZZAUTOTEST Line 2"), Add Technician {User-A}, Labor Rate {Rate-A}, Estimated Time 1.00, Tech Time 1.00, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close. On the new line click Story, type a short story and click Update. Click Complete on the new line (if a window offers Complete All Lines or asks for Mileage, finish it there), then click Mark Reviewed. Click the Finance tab and write down how it shows the first invoice. Click Create Invoice, close the New Customer Payment window without paying, and write down the new Subtotal. Open Reports > Sales again (Date: This week) and write down the rows and the Totals row Subtotal. Open Reports > Advisor Analysis again (Date: This week, no advisor chosen) and write down the rows and the Totals row. Click Parts > Part Sales > New Part Sale and try to invoice the sale without choosing a customer. If the screen insists on a customer, stop this step. Open the release notes page and find the Dashboard note that starts "Sales report totals can change".
exp: Expected results Steps 3 and 5: Before the void, the Sales report lists the invoice and its Totals row Subtotal is the amount you wrote down (for example $200.00). Advisor Analysis shows Hrs Worked 2.00, Hrs Invoiced 2.00 and Billing Efficiency 100.00% (2.00 / 2.00 x 100). Steps 10 and 11: Write down how the Finance tab marks the first invoice (for example a Void label) and the new Subtotal (for example $300.00 = $200.00 + 1.00 hour x $100.00). These two readings are records, not pass or fail points. Step 12: The Sales report lists only the new invoice: the voided invoice is gone, and the Totals row Subtotal equals the new Subtotal (for example $300.00), not the two added together (for example $500.00 = $200.00 + $300.00). Step 13: Advisor Analysis shows one row for {Work-order-1}, the new invoice, with Hrs Invoiced 3.00 (2.00 + 1.00) and the new Subtotal (for example $300.00). Hrs Worked stays 2.00, so Billing Efficiency reads 150.00% (3.00 / 2.00 x 100). The figures moved up: this is the void-then-reinvoice case. Step 14: If you could invoice a sale with no customer, it appears in the Sales report total and in Advisor Analysis. If the screen insisted on a customer, write "no-customer invoice not reachable by hand" in the result comment. Step 15: The note says Sales report totals can change for some past dates: voided invoices are no longer counted, which lowers a total; invoices with no customer attached are now included, which raises one; and a voided invoice that was invoiced again counts only the new amount. It also says the Service Advisor Analysis report changes the same way and walk-in sales now count toward advisor figures. This checks the published notes, not the product screens. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (Story 3, Measure Formulas and Report Parity); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850, version 48 (14 Oct 2026, 17:09 UTC, Chris Ward), S3-E2 and its context notes (unchanged since version 42); read 14 Oct 2026. Release notes, Confluence 931069964 (version 7) and 928121200 (version 6), Dashboard "Worth knowing" note, changed on 14 Oct 2026 (15:07 UTC) by Chris Ward in answer to our question 2 of 14 Oct 2026; read 14 Oct 2026. Dashboard v1 Technical Implementation Plan (16 Sep 2026), NFR-010; it informs and never overrules the PRD. The note first published on 9 Oct 2026 said totals "can drop"; the note as changed on 14 Oct 2026 says they "can change", and we take the later note as prevailing. Source-verified 14 October 2026. This version of the case has not yet been checked against a build (the previous version was last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026).
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S3-E2: “A voided invoice is excluded from every figure the dashboard shows. It contributes nothing to Revenue or to the parts-versus-labor split, nothing to invoiced hours or invoiced technician hours, and it is counted in neither the Sales by Customer count nor the At Risk Customers count, including when deciding a customer's most recent invoice. This is not a dashboard rule of its own: it is what the reports do, and the dashboard matches them (S3-R1). A void means the document was undone, so a figure that still carried its money or its hours would overstate the shop.” S3-E2 context note (Sales report): “That is a defect in the Sales report rather than a dashboard decision, and it is corrected inside this project so Revenue can match it (@chris ruling, 2026-09-15). Correcting it moves the Sales report's own existing totals for any range containing voided or no-company invoices, so it ships with a release note.” S3-E2 context note (Service Advisor Analysis): “Service Advisor Analysis is a direct copy of the Sales report's invoice query and carries both flaws, so it is corrected in this project too (@chris ruling, 2026-09-16: the figures need to match each other and to be right, and today they are neither). That moves advisor revenue and ELR down for periods containing voided invoices and adds walk-in sales to advisor figures, under the same release note.” Tech plan NFR-010: “Both report corrections ship with one plain-language release note: Sales report totals move for ranges containing voided or no-company invoices, and on Service Advisor Analysis revenue, ELR *and the hours columns, and therefore Labor Efficiency %* move for those periods, while advisor figures gain walk-in sales. It must also call out the void-then-reinvoice case, where a figure can move *up*” Release notes, Dashboard, Worth knowing (Confluence 931069964 v7 and 928121200 v6, 14 Oct 2026): “Sales report totals can change for some past dates. Voided invoices are no longer counted, which lowers a total, and invoices with no customer attached are now included, which raises one. A voided invoice that was invoiced again counts only the new amount. The Service Advisor Analysis report changes the same way, and walk-in sales now count toward advisor figures. Expect questions about this.” Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026. AUTOMATION: READY

title: Revenue tile shows the exact amount to the cent and equals the Sales report
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions User: you are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports). Location: you are in a quiet test location: nobody else invoices, issues credits or clocks time there this week; on the Dashboard, the Revenue tile on This Week reads $0.00 with 0 Invoices. Timing: you run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record you create stays inside This Week. Data: a test customer with one contact and one asset that uses that contact (for example ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer 1, contact Dana Test, unit ZZ-101). Data: an in-stock inventory part with a Sell price (for example $200.00). Data: Invoice 1 for that customer (not sent, not paid): one approved labor line (for example 10.00 hours at a rate from the list) and a flat Discount (for example $100.00). You have written down its Subtotal (before any discount and before tax). Data: Invoice 2 for the same customer (not sent, not paid): one approved labor line (for example 2.00 hours) with the part from 5 added (quantity 1, In stock). You have written down its Subtotal. Data: a credit on invoice 2 that returns the part, Outcome Store Credit. You have written down its amount before tax.
steps: Work out Revenue by hand: invoice 1 subtotal + invoice 2 subtotal - the credit = $1,250.00 + $480.00 - $200.00 = $1,530.00 (use your own figures if they differ). Click Dashboard in the top menu. On the Revenue tile click the range pill and choose This Week. Write down the Revenue figure exactly as shown. Click the arrow icon beside "Revenue" on the tile (its tooltip names the report). On the Sales report, make sure the Date control shows This week. If it does not, choose This week. Write down the Subtotal in the Totals row at the bottom of the table.
exp: Expected results Steps 1 and 4: The Revenue figure equals your hand total exactly. With the example data it reads $1,530.00 ($1,250.00 + $480.00 - $200.00): the $100.00 discount is not taken off and the tax is not added. Step 4: The figure shows dollars and cents (e.g. $1,530.00), not a rounded whole-dollar amount. Steps 4 and 7: The Sales report for the same location and the same week shows the same amount in its Totals row Subtotal as the Revenue tile. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3), story SV-9576 (S4); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v48, read 14 Oct 2026, S3 (S3-R1, S3-R2 Revenue row, context note), S4 (S4-R2). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, as re-shared and read 14 Oct 2026; 02_Last12_After and 03_Range_After re-shot from the SV-490 build on 14 Oct 2026, the other captured from the SV-8311 build on 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 02_Last12_After, 03_Range_After, 10_sales_After.
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S3-R2: “Each measure is calculated as defined in the table below.” S3-R2 table row (Revenue): “| Revenue | Sum of invoice subtotals in the selected range, before any discount and before tax, minus credit memos. Shown to the cent. | Sales report |” S4-R2: “The Revenue tile headline is the total revenue for the selected range, shown as a dollar amount to the cent.” S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.” S3 context note (parity check): “to check parity on a KPI tile that shows a shop-wide figure, compare it against the matching report with all advisors or all technicians selected (no filter applied).” Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026. AUTOMATION: READY

title: Revenue tile leaves out a reversed or voided invoice, like the Sales report
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions User: you are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports). Location: you are in a fresh test location made for this run, so nothing else is invoiced, credited or clocked there; on the Dashboard, the Revenue tile on This Week reads $0.00 with 0 Invoices. Timing: you run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record you create stays inside This Week. Data: a test customer with one contact and one asset that uses that contact (for example ZZAUTOTEST Dash Customer 1, contact Dana Test, unit ZZ-101). People (Advisor A): you (Admin ShopView); the Service Advisor in the work order's left panel shows your name by default. Data: Three invoiced work orders A, B and C (not sent, not paid) for that customer, Service Advisor Advisor A, each with one labor line at $100.00 an hour: A 3.00 hours, B 5.00 hours, C 2.00 hours (Tech Time the same). You have written down each Subtotal (e.g. A $300.00, B $500.00, C $200.00).
