Click Work Orders, open work order B, click the Finance tab, click the invoice's three dots > Reverse, and confirm Reverse. Click Dashboard, set Revenue to This Week again and write down the figure. Click Work Orders and open work order C. On the Lines tab click New Line: What Are You Doing? "ZZAUTOTEST Extra", Labor Rate = the $100 rate you added in this location (for example ZZAUTOTEST Rate 100), Estimated Time 0.50, Tech Time 0.50, tick Line Approved > Save & Close. (This voids C's unpaid invoice.) On the new line click Story > type a short story > Update, then click Complete (if a window offers Complete All Lines or asks for Mileage, finish it there), then click Mark Reviewed. Click the Finance tab and write down what it shows for C's first invoice (for example a Void label). Click Create Invoice, close the New Customer Payment dialog without paying, and write down the new Subtotal (e.g. $250.00 = $200.00 + 0.50 hour x $100.00). Click Dashboard, set Revenue to This Week and write down the figure. Click the arrow icon beside "Revenue" on the tile (its tooltip names the report). On the Sales report set the Date control to This week and write down every invoice row and the Totals row Subtotal. Try to make an invoice with no customer: Parts > Part Sales > New Part Sale, and see whether it can be invoiced without choosing a customer. If the screen insists on a customer, stop this step.
exp: Expected results Step 1: Revenue reads $1,000.00 ($300.00 + $500.00 + $200.00). Step 3: After reversing B: Revenue reads $500.00 ($300.00 + $200.00). The reversed invoice adds nothing. Step 9: After voiding C's first invoice and re-invoicing: Revenue reads $550.00 ($300.00 + $250.00). The voided $200.00 invoice adds nothing and the new $250.00 invoice counts. Step 11: The Sales report for This week lists A and C's new invoice only (no row for B and none for C's voided invoice), and its Totals row Subtotal reads $550.00, the same as the tile. Step 12: If you could invoice a sale with no customer, its subtotal is in both the Revenue figure and the Sales report total. If you could not, write "no-customer invoice not reachable by hand" in the result comment. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v48, read 14 Oct 2026, S3 (S3-E2 and its context note, S3-R1). Tech plan section 7 (2026-09-16) informs how a void is produced by hand: Reverse removes the invoice, and a line added to a still-unpaid invoiced work order voids it.
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S3-E2: “A voided invoice is excluded from every figure the dashboard shows. It contributes nothing to Revenue or to the parts-versus-labor split, nothing to invoiced hours or invoiced technician hours, and it is counted in neither the Sales by Customer count nor the At Risk Customers count, including when deciding a customer's most recent invoice. This is not a dashboard rule of its own: it is what the reports do, and the dashboard matches them (S3-R1). A void means the document was undone, so a figure that still carried its money or its hours would overstate the shop.” S3-R1: “Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.” S3-E2 context note (Sales report): “That is a defect in the Sales report rather than a dashboard decision, and it is corrected inside this project so Revenue can match it (@chris ruling, 2026-09-15). Correcting it moves the Sales report's own existing totals for any range containing voided or no-company invoices, so it ships with a release note.” Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026. src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S4-R3: “The Revenue tile shows a supporting line reading "Parts {parts}% · Labor {labor}% · Other {other}%", each percent a whole number of the tile’s revenue. title: At Risk Customers counts the right customers for the chosen days
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions User: you are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports). Location: you are in a location (workplace) with several months of invoice history (many customers, invoices going back more than a year). At Risk needs old invoices, which cannot be back-dated by hand. Data (Customer W): in the At Risk table (window 120 Days), a customer with Lifetime Invoices 2 or more, whose newest invoice you will make and then undo. You have written down W's Last Invoice Date. Data (Customer X): a customer whose only invoice is more than 12 months old (Lifetime Invoices 1, so Revenue (12 Mo) is $0.00). Data (Customer Y): a customer with 2 or more invoices, all more than 12 months old.
steps: On the At Risk Customers tile click the window pill and choose 120 Days. Write down the headline and count the table rows. Look for customer X in the table. Look for customer Y in the table. Read down the table and check every row: Lifetime Invoices is 2 or more, or Revenue (12 Mo) is above $0.00. Window edge: on the window pill try each of 30, 60, 90, 120 and 180 Days, and look for a customer whose Last Invoice Date is exactly that many days before today (count calendar days, e.g. Jun 9, 2026 to Oct 7, 2026 = 120 days) and one at one day fewer. If the Create Invoice step on a work order lets you choose the invoice date, you may make such invoices instead. Make a new invoice today for customer W: Work Orders > Create Work Order > W and its asset > Save; in New Line one labor line (e.g. Labor Rate EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time 1), tick Line Approved > Save & Close; Story > Update; Complete (finish any Missing Details window); Mark Reviewed; Finance > Create Invoice (close the New Customer Payment window without paying). Click Dashboard, set the window to 120 Days and write down the headline. Look for W in the table. Click Work Orders, open the work order you just invoiced, Finance tab > the invoice's three dots > Reverse > confirm. Click Dashboard, set the window to 120 Days, write down the headline and find W's row.
exp: Expected results Step 1: The headline is a plain number (e.g. 12, no words, no dollar sign) and equals the number of rows in the table. Steps 2 and 3: Customer X (one invoice, $0.00 revenue in the last 12 months) is not listed. Customer Y (2 or more invoices, $0.00 recent revenue) is listed. Step 4: Every listed customer has Lifetime Invoices of 2 or more, or Revenue (12 Mo) above $0.00. Step 5: Window edge: a customer whose newest invoice is exactly the chosen number of days old is listed, and one at one day fewer is not. If no such pair exists and invoice dates cannot be chosen, write "window edge not reachable by hand" in the result comment. Step 7: After invoicing W today, W leaves the list and the headline drops by 1 (e.g. 12 to 11). Step 9: After reversing that new invoice, W is back with its earlier Last Invoice Date and the headline returns to the step 1 figure: the undone invoice is ignored when deciding W's newest invoice. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3), story SV-9577 (S5); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v48, read 14 Oct 2026, S5 (S5-R15, S5-R7), S3 (S3-E2). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, as re-shared and read 14 Oct 2026; screenshots of the SV-490 build re-shot on 14 Oct 2026) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 09_AtRisk_After (table: Customer, Last Invoice Date, Lifetime Invoices, Revenue (12 Mo)), 09_AtRisk_Window.
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S5-R15: “Two parts of the at-risk definition are fixed here so the count cannot be read two ways. "Some revenue in the last twelve months" means revenue greater than $0.00 over the trailing twelve months, measured the way the Revenue tile measures revenue: invoice subtotals before any discount and before tax, minus credit memos. A customer whose twelve-month revenue is exactly $0.00, or is negative because credits exceeded sales, does not satisfy this part of the test, though they can still qualify on the two-or-more-lifetime-invoices part. "At least the selected number of days old" is counted in whole calendar days in the selected workplace's timezone, from the date of the customer's most recent invoice to the current date. The count therefore changes at the shop's own midnight and is stable through the shop's working day, and two people viewing the same workplace from different places see the same number.” S5-R7: “The At Risk Customers tile headline is the count of at-risk customers for the selected inactivity window, shown as a plain number.” S3-E2: “A voided invoice is excluded from every figure the dashboard shows. It contributes nothing to Revenue or to the parts-versus-labor split, nothing to invoiced hours or invoiced technician hours, and it is counted in neither the Sales by Customer count nor the At Risk Customers count, including when deciding a customer's most recent invoice. This is not a dashboard rule of its own: it is what the reports do, and the dashboard matches them (S3-R1). A void means the document was undone, so a figure that still carried its money or its hours would overstate the shop.” Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026. AUTOMATION: READY

title: At Risk trend line has twelve monthly points and the last equals the count
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), whose role has the Reports permission and can reverse an invoice, at location {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). Your browser window is at least 1024 pixels wide at 100% zoom (a maximised laptop or desktop window). {Location-A} has invoices going back more than a year, with many customers. The At Risk Customers tile's window pill reads 120 Days. Customer {Customer-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Lapsed Fleet) is at risk on 120 days: its newest invoice, on work order {Work-order-1} (for example S490-1180), is 2 to 6 months old, and it also has an older invoice. {Work-order-1}'s invoice has no payment, so it can be reversed.
steps: Click Dashboard in the top bar. Take a screenshot of the At Risk Customers tile and read its headline. Count the points on the At Risk Customers trend line, from left to right. Hover over each point and write down the month and the value it shows. Click Work Orders, open {Work-order-1}, click the Finance tab, click the invoice's three dots, click Reverse and confirm. Click Dashboard in the top bar and check the At Risk Customers pill still reads 120 Days. Hover over each point again, write down the month and the value, and read the headline.
exp: Expected results Step 3: The trend line has twelve points, one per month, for the last twelve months. Step 4: The right-most point's value equals the headline from step 2 (for example both 12). Step 7: At least one earlier month's value differs from what you wrote down in step 4, not only the last one: every point is worked out again from today's data rather than kept from the past. Step 7: The right-most point's value still equals the headline. Steps 4 and 7: If the points show no value when you hover them, the values cannot be checked by hand, because the line's height does not show the count (each tile draws its line between its own lowest and highest point). Write "point values not checked by hand" in the result comment and mark the case Blocked. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9577 (Story 5, Count Tiles), with SV-9576 (Story 4); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850, version 48 (14 Oct 2026, 17:09 UTC, Chris Ward), S5-R13 (unchanged since version 42) and S4-R11b (added in version 45 on 14 Oct 2026 (15:06 UTC) by Chris Ward, from Chris Ward's answer 1 of 14 Oct 2026 to our question sheet; the spec's change log (version 46) lists it under 2026-10-14); read 14 Oct 2026. Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge) boards 01_Opens_After and 09_AtRisk_After, used for on-screen labels only. Source-verified 14 October 2026. This version of the case has not yet been checked against a build (the previous version was last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026).
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S5-R13: “The At Risk Customers sparkline shows the at-risk count over the trailing twelve months as twelve monthly points. Each historical point is the at-risk count as of the last day of that month in the workplace's timezone, using the inactivity window the tile currently shows. The twelfth point is computed as of now, rather than as of a month end that has not happened yet, so it always equals the headline. Every point is recomputed from current data, so a later void changes the past points: recording the count as it stood at the time would contradict S3-E2, which excludes a voided invoice even when deciding a customer's most recent invoice.” S4-R11b: “The sparkline shows direction, not level. Each tile scales its line between its own lowest and highest point, so a figure that never changes over the range (for example Technician Utilization at 100% on every day) draws as a flat line along the bottom of the trend area, whatever the figure is. The headline carries the actual value. The start-at-0 axis of S9-R8 applies to the expanded and report charts, which have an axis, not to the sparkline.” Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026. AUTOMATION: READY

title: Ratio tiles with no hours show a grey dash, never 0.00%
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions User: you are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports). Location: you are in a fresh test location made for this run, with no clocked time and no invoices this week (you check this in step 1). Timing: you run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record you create stays inside This Week. People (Technician 1): a test technician in this run's location, with Time Clock on and a department whose time clock is on (for internal, non work order time), whose sign-in you have.
steps: Click Dashboard in the top menu. Set the range pill to This Week on Revenue, Billing Efficiency, Technician Efficiency and Technician Utilization. Write down each tile's headline, its colour and the line under it. Click the arrow icon beside "Technician Efficiency", set the report's Date control to This week, and write down how the report shows an empty value. In the private window, signed in as Technician 1, click Clock In in the top bar, choose the department (not a work order), and clock out. In Reports > Timesheet Activities edit that record so it runs exactly 1.00 hour earlier today (e.g. 9:00 AM to 10:00 AM). If it cannot be edited, use the hours shown there. Click Dashboard, set Technician Utilization to This Week and write down the headline and the line under it.
exp: Expected results Step 3: Billing Efficiency, Technician Efficiency and Technician Utilization each read a single hyphen "-" in grey. None reads "0.00%", none is blank and none shows an error. Step 3: Revenue reads $0.00 with "0 Invoices" under it, because there is no parts-and-labor split to show. Step 4: The report may show its own empty value differently (for example an empty number with the % sign). That difference is expected and is not a failure. Step 7: After 1.00 hour of internal time only, Technician Utilization reads "0.00%" with "0.00 WO Hrs / 1.00 Clocked" under it (0.00 / (0.00 + 1.00) x 100 = 0.00): a real zero, shown differently from the "-" of no hours. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3), story SV-9576 (S4); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v48, read 14 Oct 2026, S3 (S3-E3 and its context note), S4 (S4-N2, S4-R9). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, as re-shared and read 14 Oct 2026; a screenshot of the SV-490 build re-shot on 14 Oct 2026) row 15 (board 15_Empty_After): ratio tiles read a grey "-". Boards used for labels only.
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S3-E3: “Billing Efficiency, Technician Efficiency and Technician Utilization are each a ratio. When the denominator for the selected range is zero, worked hours, clocked hours, or the sum of work-order and internal hours, the measure has no value for that range. It is not zero, and the tile must not show "0.00%", because no hours recorded and a genuine zero percent are different facts. The same applies to the Revenue tile's parts-versus-labor split when revenue for the range is zero (S4-N2 already gives that tile its fallback supporting line). Inside the Technician Efficiency calculation, a work order line with invoiced technician time but no clocked time contributes no split share rather than an infinite one. The tile headline reads exactly "-", a single hyphen, in grey.” S3-E3 context note: “the matching report renders its own empty cell differently, as an empty number with the percent sign still shown. Bringing the report's empty state into line is deliberately outside this spec, so a difference between the tile and the report in this one case, where neither is showing a figure, is not a failure of the parity rule in S3-R1.” S4-N2: “If the Revenue tile has no parts-versus-labor split to show, its supporting line reads "{count} Invoices" instead.” S4-R9: “The Technician Utilization tile shows a supporting line reading "{work-order hours} WO Hrs / {clocked hours} Clocked".” Last checked against build v26.40.8-754bd3a on 10/13/2026. title: Trend line splits the range by day, week or month correctly
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), whose role has the Reports permission, at location {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). Your browser window is at least 1024 pixels wide at 100% zoom (a maximised laptop or desktop window). {Location-A} has invoices on most days of the last twelve months, so Revenue has a value in every period. Day {Day-A} (for example a Sunday this month) has no clocked time at {Location-A}, while the day before and the day after it do. Day {Day-B} (for example a Saturday) has clocked time at {Location-A}, and the day after it, {Day-C}, has none.
steps: Click Dashboard in the top bar. Click the Revenue tile's date pill, pick a start day and an end day so the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 31 days" and click Apply. Hover along the Revenue trend line, or count its points, and write down how many points there are and the date each shows. Click the Revenue pill again, pick a start day and an end day so the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 32 days" and click Apply, and do the same. Do the same with a range of 182 days, then with a range of 183 days. Set a 31-day range again, hover one point and write down its date and value. Click Reports in the top bar, click Sales, set the Date control to that single day and read the Totals row Subtotal. Go back to the Dashboard and set the Technician Utilization tile to a custom range from the day before {Day-A} to the day after {Day-A}. Look at the Technician Utilization trend line around {Day-A}. Set the Technician Utilization tile to a custom range from {Day-B} to {Day-C} and look at where the trend line would be.
exp: Expected results Steps 3 and 4: 31 days: one point per day (31 points). 32 days: one point per week. Step 5: 182 days: one point per week. 183 days: one point per month. Steps 6 and 7: The hovered day's value equals the Sales report's Totals row Subtotal for that day. Step 9: {Day-A} leaves a gap in the line: the line is not joined across it and does not drop to zero. Step 10: With only one day that has a value, no line is drawn. In its place the tile shows the empty-chart placeholder: a light grey dashed outline with rounded corners, no fill and a grey line-chart icon in the middle, the same height as a trend line. The headline still shows its figure. Steps 3 to 7: If the trend line shows no dates or values when you hover it, count the points instead (zoom the browser in if needed) and write "values not checked by hand" in the result comment for steps 6 and 7. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9576 (Story 4, KPI Hero Tiles), with SV-9579 (Story 7) and SV-9575 (Story 3); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850, version 48 (14 Oct 2026, 17:09 UTC, Chris Ward), S4-R11, S4-R12, S4-R15, S4-R16, S4-R18 and S3-R1 (unchanged since version 42) and S7-R2a (added in version 45 on 14 Oct 2026 (15:06 UTC) by Chris Ward; the spec's change log (version 46) lists it under 2026-10-14); read 14 Oct 2026. The 731-day and 732-day ranges were removed because a tile's calendar now allows at most 366 days (S7-R2a, Chris Ward's answer 3 of 14 Oct 2026). Design canvas board 03_Range_After (calendar, "Range: N days" readout, Apply) and row 15 (empty-chart placeholder, approved 7 Oct 2026). Source-verified 14 October 2026. This version of the case has not yet been checked against a build (the previous version was last checked against build v26.40.8-754bd3a on 10/13/2026).
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S4-R11: “The sparkline draws one point per bucket, and the bucket size is chosen from the length of the selected range: a range of 31 days or fewer buckets by day; 32 to 182 days by week; 183 to 731 days by month; anything longer by quarter. Each point is the measure recomputed over that bucket using the same calculation as the headline, so a point can never disagree with the tile it sits in. A bucket for which the measure has no value (S3-E3) contributes no point, and interior gaps are preserved rather than closed up or drawn as zero. title: Tile figure, trend line and expanded table all add up to the same numbers
pre: Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session) Preconditions User: you are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports). steps: Click Dashboard in the top menu. The four top tiles open on This Month. On Technician Efficiency write down the headline and the line under it (e.g. 377.58 Invoiced Tech Hrs / 858.45 Clocked). Click View details on Technician Efficiency. Page through the table and add up the Clocked Hrs column and the Invoiced Tech Hrs column. Work out Invoiced / Clocked x 100 from your sums. On Technician Utilization click View details. Add up WO Hours, Internal Hours and Total Hours. On Billing Efficiency click View details. Add up Worked Hours and Invoiced Hrs. exp: Expected results Steps 2, 3 and 4: Technician Efficiency: the Clocked Hrs sum equals the Clocked figure, the Invoiced Tech Hrs sum equals the Invoiced Tech Hrs figure, and your Invoiced / Clocked x 100 equals the headline. Step 6: Billing Efficiency: the Worked Hours sum equals the Clocked figure and the Invoiced Hrs sum equals the Invoiced figure. Step 7: Revenue: the chart's bars add up to the headline. Steps 3 to 7: The chart and table cover the same range as the tile (This Month), and no point or row contradicts the tile. Step 8: Each trend line stops at today: there are no points for the days of the month still to come, so the line and the headline cover the same part of the month. title: Revenue tile shows shop supplies as an Other share
pre: Preconditions You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports). You are in location {Location-A}, where nothing else is invoiced, credited or clocked this week. On the Dashboard, the Revenue tile on This Week reads $0.00 with "0 Invoices". For example: {Location-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C614718 Other Shop. Customer {Customer-A} has one asset, {Unit-A}. For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C614718 Other Fleet and {Unit-A} is ZZ-C614718-1. Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} and {Unit-A} is reviewed and not invoiced. It has one approved labor line, {Line-1}, of 3.00 hours at $100.00 an hour, one part, {Part-A}, with Sell Price $100.00, and shop supplies of 10% of labor. For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-15500, {Line-1} is ZZAUTOTEST C614718 Line 1 and {Part-A} is ZZAUTOTEST-C614718-P1. Starting screen: the Dashboard at {Location-A}. If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
steps: Click Work Orders in the top menu and open {Work-order-1}. Click the Finance tab and click Create Invoice. Close the New Customer Payment dialog without paying. On the invoice, read the Labor, Parts, Shop Supplies and Subtotal amounts. Click Dashboard in the top menu and set the Revenue tile's date range to This Week. Read the Revenue headline. Read the line under the Revenue headline. Click the report arrow beside the Revenue tile's name. In the Sales report, read the Labor column figure for this range.
exp: Expected results Step 1: {Work-order-1} opens. Step 2: The invoice is created and the New Customer Payment dialog opens. Step 3: The dialog closes and the invoice stays unpaid. Step 4: The invoice shows Labor $300.00, Parts $100.00, Shop Supplies $30.00 and Subtotal $430.00 (for example). Write the four amounts down. Step 5: The Revenue tile shows This Week. Step 6: Revenue reads the invoice Subtotal, to the cent (for example $430.00). Step 7: The line reads "Parts 23% · Labor 70% · Other 7%" (for example). Parts = 100 ÷ 430 = 23.3%, so 23. Labor = 300 ÷ 430 = 69.8%, so 70. Other = the shop supplies, 30 ÷ 430 = 7.0%, so 7. Each is a whole number, the three add up to 100, and the shop supplies are not counted in Labor. Step 8: The Sales report opens on the same dates (This Week). Step 9: The Labor column shows the invoice's labor only (for example $300.00), the same labor figure the tile's Labor share is worked out from. Source — where this behaviour comes from Epic SV-490; story SV-9576 (Story 4, KPI Hero Tiles), story SV-9575 (Story 3, Measure Formulas), story SV-9582 (Story 10, Report Drill-In); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v50 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 16 Oct 2026, S4-R3 (reworded in v50 after Ayesha Khan's question of 16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward's ruling in the PRD Change Log), S3-R2 table (Revenue row), S10-R1. Source-verified 16 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build.
src: Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility) S3-R2 table: Revenue: “Revenue | Sum of invoice subtotals in the selected range, before any discount and before tax, minus credit memos. Shown to the cent. | Sales report” S4-R3: “The Revenue tile shows a supporting line reading "Parts {parts}% · Labor {labor}% · Other {other}%", each percent a whole number of the tile’s revenue. Parts is parts sales, net of credits (as today). Labor is labor sales only, the same figure as the Sales report’s Labor column. Other is everything else in revenue: shop supplies, fees and any other line that is neither a part nor labor. The three are rounded so they always add up to 100. "· Other {other}%" is left off when Other rounds to 0%, so a shop with no supplies or fees reads "Parts {parts}% · Labor {labor}%".” S10-R1: “Each KPI tile and the Sales by Customer tile shows a report link.” AUTOMATION: HOLD - not yet build-verified
